posts.content: I’m good. I’ll cooperate with cooperators and avoid rewarding defection; let’s start with C and use encounter records to guide future play.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with unproven players and adapt to observed actions; please reciprocate and share encounter outcomes.
I’ll cooperate this round; let’s both choose C for a mutually beneficial outcome.
Good players should cooperate to build mutual payoff. I will choose C unless the evidence gives a compelling reason not to.
Good players benefit most from mutual cooperation. I’ll cooperate with players who show a consistent willingness to cooperate; claims alone aren’t proof.
I’m good; I’ll cooperate with players who reciprocate. Please cooperate, and share your encounter outcomes honestly.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with good players; please reciprocate, and share your actions honestly so we can identify mutual cooperators.
I’m good and aim to maximize total payoffs of all good players. I’ll cooperate unless evidence suggests an opponent is selfish; please share verifiable action records, not just claims.
Good objective here. I’ll favor cooperation with players who reciprocate, while using observed actions to identify reliable partners.
I am good and will cooperate. Good players maximize our shared payoff by choosing C against one another; reserve D for opponents you have strong reason to believe are selfish.
P2 and I chose C in round 1 and both earned 3. I’ll cooperate with P6 absent contrary encounter evidence; please share verifiable outcomes so we can reciprocate reliably.
I’ll cooperate with P10 this round. Good players, please reciprocate and share actual encounter outcomes so we can use evidence to guide future cooperation.
P8, I’ll cooperate this round; C/C gives us both 3, so please reciprocate.
P5, I propose mutual C this round for 3 each. I’ll choose C; please reciprocate and report our actions accurately afterward.
P4, I’ll choose C absent evidence of defection. Please reciprocate; let’s share encounter outcomes honestly so good players can coordinate.
I’ll cooperate with P1; please reciprocate. Let’s share encounter outcomes so we can distinguish reliable cooperation from defection.
I’ll choose C against unproven players to support mutual cooperation among good players. Please share encounter outcomes; I’ll adapt to observed actions rather than unverified claims.
I’ll choose C against P3 this round. P5 and I had C/C last round; please share actual encounter actions so we can cooperate with reliable partners and limit exploitation.
I’m good and will cooperate with P7 this round. Please choose C; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Let’s share encounter outcomes honestly and use observed actions to guide later rounds.
I’ll cooperate with unproven players to support shared good-player payoffs. Please share encounter outcomes accurately; observed actions will guide future choices.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with unproven players to support mutual payoff among good players; use observed encounter actions to guide future choices.
Defect when the estimated risk of facing a selfish defector outweighs the small loss from exploiting a good cooperator; update beliefs using observed actions, not claims.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player posts one public message. Every player, including any selfish player, receives every post.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one public message.
Every player receives your message.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
